title: Moderate trump, two side Aces
author_notes: EC-055 checkpoint-3 coverage: a second bid_sizing scenario, deliberately weaker than bid_training_012's near-solid six-card Spade run. Only King-Queen head this five-card Heart suit, but two side Aces (Spades, Diamonds) give near-certain outside winners a single-suit sizing question rarely has. Single trump offered (Hearts), so the decision is purely how many tricks this specific combination of moderate trump control and side-suit Aces supports. Independent hand; ratings are authored judgments, not probabilities or guaranteed outcomes.

feedback.title: Safe, but the two Aces are doing nothing extra
feedback.summary: Four is secure from King-Queen of Hearts and the two side Aces alone, without needing anything further from this hand.
points: Control: King-Queen of Hearts lead the trump suit; the Spade and Diamond Aces are near-certain side winners if opponents can follow.
This target does not need either low Heart to be promoted by length.
A stronger target is defensible from three separate sources of strength; four is not wrong, just conservative.

feedback.title: Trump control plus two side Aces
feedback.summary: Five combines the King-Queen trump lead with both side Aces, three separate sources rather than one long suit alone.
points: Control: King-Queen of Hearts as trump, plus the Ace of Spades and the Ace of Diamonds as side winners.
Unlike a single strong suit, this target draws on three different sources of strength rather than one holding stretching to cover it.
This does not guarantee five tricks; it reflects that three separate cards support this target rather than one alone.

feedback.title: The low Hearts still need to be promoted
feedback.summary: Six needs one of the remaining low Hearts to become a winner by length, on top of both side Aces already holding.
points: King-Queen and the two Aces support five; a sixth trick asks the low Hearts to do more than follow suit.
Five cards in the trump suit is moderate length, not a long run that reliably promotes low cards.
This is not an unreasonable attempt, but it depends on more than the visible strength guarantees.
